title: agent-budget-semantics: Differential Testing of Budget Enforcement Across AI Agent Frameworks
description: Differential testing of budget enforcement across 11 AI agent frameworks against a deterministic mock language model with a request ledger. Same underlying workload (four LLM calls, three tool calls, 478 tokens) produces four distinct gen_ai.agent.iteration_budget.consumed values across enforcing frameworks. Pre-run source-code readings agreed with runtime for exactly half of the executed frameworks. A synthetic per-iteration chargeback rate applied uniformly across the framework-reported counts diverges by up to 2.6363x (0.33834 against 0.12834 on the reference workload); the chargeback rate is a constructed pricing model rather than any vendor rate card, and the divergence is a property of the counting disagreement rather than an observed bill. The v0.5.0 deposit description gave this spread as 2.3x, which was the ratio of an illustrative worked example conflated with the measured value; see ERRATA.md entry E1 in the repository, since a minted description cannot be edited. One executed framework (Agno 1.2.5) accepts a tool_call_limit that its outer loop does not respect, producing runtime paths without framework-supplied bound. Findings support recording iteration_budget.limit verbatim without cross-framework normalization; the OpenTelemetry spec PR carrying a shared iteration_budget attribute set (semantic-conventions-genai #439) was withdrawn on 2026-08-27 after maintainer review concluded the counts are not comparable across implementations, and this work treats that negative result as the finding.
